{{short description|American mathematician}}
{{about||the American psychologist|E. Mark Stern}}
'''Mark A. Stern''' is an American [[mathematician]] whose focus has been on [[geometric analysis]], [[Yang–Mills theory]], [[Hodge theory]], and [[string theory]].

One of Stern's foremost accomplishments is his proof (joint with Leslie D. Saper) of the [[Zucker conjecture]] concerning locally symmetric spaces.<ref name="auto">{{cite web|url=http://www.science.tamu.edu/giving/adfs.php|title=- College of Science, Texas A&M University|first=College of Science Communications, Texas A&M|last=University|date=26 May 2005|website=Science.tamu.edu|accessdate=12 August 2017}}</ref> Since about 2000, Stern has focused on geometric problems arising in [[physics]], ranging from [[harmonic]] theory to string theory and [[supersymmetry]].

Stern has taught at [[Duke University]] since 1985, and was promoted to [[professor]] in 1992. He has been the mathematics department [[chairman]] but has focused primarily on research and teaching, with major grant support from the [[National Science Foundation]]. At Duke, he teaches such courses as [[multivariable calculus]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://services.math.duke.edu/~stern/teaching/mth103/|title=Math 103, Spring 1999|website=services.math.duke.edu|accessdate=12 August 2017}}</ref>

Since 2010, Stern has spoken to advanced math audiences at the [[Newton Institute]], [[CUNY Graduate Center]], [[U.C. Irvine]], [[Johns Hopkins University|Johns Hopkins]], the [[University of Maryland]], and multiple academic groups.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fds.duke.edu/db/aas/math/faculty/stern/cv.html|title=Curriculum Vitae of Mark A. Stern|website=fds.duke.edu|accessdate=12 August 2017}}</ref>

==Academic background==
Prior to Duke, Stern was a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] at [[Princeton, New Jersey|Princeton]], where he received his Ph.D. in 1985. His thesis advisor was [[S.T. Yau]]. Stern studied math at [[Texas A&M]], where he received his B.S. degree in 1980, before moving to Princeton. Stern grew up in Dallas, where he graduated from [[St. Mark's School of Texas]].

Stern is a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] and has won an [[Alfred P. Sloan]] Fellowship and a Presidential Young Investigator Award.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://math.duke.edu/people/mark-stern|title=Mark A. Stern - Department of Mathematics|website=math.duke.edu|accessdate=12 August 2017}}</ref><ref name="duke.edu">{{cite web|url=https://scholars.duke.edu/display/per9873252|title=Mark A. Stern - Scholars@Duke|website=scholars.duke.edu|accessdate=12 August 2017}}</ref><ref name="auto"/> In 2014, Stern was inducted into the Academy of Distinguished Former Students at Texas A&M.<ref name="auto"/>
